parameters.query:
-- Select leads to announce to the CRM as lead.qualified (stage A, read side).
-- p1 CRM_EVENTS_SINCE (ISO timestamp), p2 batch size, p3 protocol revision.
--
-- A lead qualifies once it has an assigned seller and was created at or after
-- CRM_EVENTS_SINCE (historic leads are never backfilled). Under 1.1 it is a
-- candidate while its requirement differs from the one its newest enqueued
-- event carried. Under 1.2 it is a candidate while the fingerprint of its raw
-- record inputs (crm_lead_source_hash) differs from the one last examined; the
-- builder then decides whether the record it would send actually changed. A
-- seller without crm_user_id blocks the lead as seller_not_mapped; mapping the
-- seller makes it a candidate on the next pass. `revision` is only a proposal:
-- Insert Lead Qualified Event re-checks it under a row lock, so concurrent
-- passes can never enqueue the same revision twice.
WITH scope AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT l.id, s.crm_user_id,
         CASE WHEN $3::text = '1.2' THEN crm_lead_source_hash(l.id) END AS source_hash
  FROM leads l
  JOIN sellers s ON s.id = l.assigned_seller_id
  WHERE l.deleted_at IS NULL
    AND l.created_at >= $1::timestamptz
    AND CASE
      WHEN $3::text = '1.2' THEN crm_lead_source_hash(l.id) IS DISTINCT FROM l.crm_checked_source_hash
      ELSE l.crm_enqueued_requirement IS DISTINCT FROM COALESCE(l.requirement, '')
    END
),
blocked AS (
  UPDATE leads l
  SET crm_blocked_reason = 'seller_not_mapped'
  FROM scope sc
  WHERE l.id = sc.id
    AND sc.crm_user_id IS NULL
    AND l.crm_blocked_reason IS DISTINCT FROM 'seller_not_mapped'
  RETURNING l.id
)
SELECT
  l.id AS lead_id,
  (
    SELECT COALESCE(MAX(e.revision), 0) + 1
    FROM crm_events e
    WHERE e.lead_id = l.id
      AND e.event_type = 'lead.qualified'
  ) AS revision,
  COALESCE(
    l.source_conversation_id,
    (
      SELECT c.id
      FROM conversations c
      WHERE c.lead_id = l.id
        AND c.deleted_at IS NULL
      ORDER BY c.id DESC
      LIMIT 1
    )
  ) AS conversation_id,
  l.phone_number,
  l.whatsapp_name,
  l.service,
  l.city,
  l.requirement,
  l.qualification_context,
  sc.crm_user_id::text AS crm_user_id,
  sc.source_hash AS crm_source_hash,
  wn.phone_number AS source_number_phone,
  -- The newest advisor decision of the lead (same lookup as the ClickUp
  -- task). Only read under 1.2, where it becomes ai_summary.
  CASE WHEN $3::text = '1.2' THEN (
    SELECT ad.output_payload
    FROM advisor_decisions ad
    LEFT JOIN conversations c_ad ON c_ad.id = ad.conversation_id
    WHERE ad.lead_id = l.id
       OR c_ad.lead_id = l.id
    ORDER BY ad.created_at DESC, ad.id DESC
    LIMIT 1
  ) END AS advisor_output_payload
FROM scope sc
JOIN leads l ON l.id = sc.id
LEFT JOIN whatsapp_numbers wn ON wn.id = l.source_number_id
WHERE sc.crm_user_id IS NOT NULL
-- Previously blocked leads (e.g. an invalid phone) go last so they cannot
-- starve fresh leads out of the batch.
ORDER BY (l.crm_blocked_reason IS NOT NULL), l.created_at, l.id
LIMIT COALESCE(NULLIF($2::text, '')::integer, 20);

-- Enqueue one lead.qualified event (stage A, write side).
-- p1 lead_id, p2 revision, p3 event_id, p4 conversation_id, p5 body,
-- p6 requirement snapshot the body was built from, p7 blocked reason,
-- p8 record hash of the body (1.2), p9 source hash the candidate was selected
-- with (1.2). p8 and p9 are empty under 1.1.
--
-- The lead row is locked first. Under 1.1 (p9 empty) the event is inserted only
-- while the lead still holds the snapshot requirement and that requirement was
-- not enqueued yet. Under 1.2 (p9 set) the lead's inputs must still match the
-- source hash the body was built from; the event is inserted only when its
-- record hash differs from the last enqueued one, and either way the source
-- hash is recorded as examined, so an input change that leaves the record
-- unchanged (or a blocked lead) is not rebuilt on every pass. In both modes p2
-- must be exactly the next revision; otherwise a concurrent pass or a newer
-- correction got there first and this item does nothing (the next pass picks up
-- whatever is left). Unique event_id and (lead_id, event_type, revision) back
-- that up, so re-running the stage never duplicates an event.
WITH target AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT
    l.id,
    l.crm_enqueued_requirement,
    l.crm_enqueued_record_hash,
    COALESCE(l.requirement, '') AS current_requirement,
    CASE WHEN NULLIF($9::text, '') IS NOT NULL THEN crm_lead_source_hash(l.id) END AS current_source_hash
  FROM leads l
  WHERE l.id = $1::bigint
    AND l.deleted_at IS NULL
  FOR UPDATE
),
expected AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT t.id, t.crm_enqueued_record_hash
  FROM target t
  WHERE CASE
      WHEN NULLIF($9::text, '') IS NULL
        THEN t.current_requirement = $6::text
          AND t.crm_enqueued_requirement IS DISTINCT FROM t.current_requirement
      ELSE t.current_source_hash = $9::text
    END
    AND (
      SELECT COALESCE(MAX(e.revision), 0)
      FROM crm_events e
      WHERE e.lead_id = t.id
        AND e.event_type = 'lead.qualified'
    ) = $2::integer - 1
),
inserted AS (
  INSERT INTO crm_events (event_id, event_type, conversation_id, lead_id, revision, body)
  SELECT $3::text, 'lead.qualified', $4::text, x.id, $2::integer, $5::text
  FROM expected x
  WHERE NULLIF($7::text, '') IS NULL
    AND (NULLIF($9::text, '') IS NULL OR x.crm_enqueued_record_hash IS DISTINCT FROM NULLIF($8::text, ''))
  ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
  RETURNING id, lead_id, event_id
),
lead_update AS (
  UPDATE leads l
  SET crm_enqueued_requirement = CASE WHEN i.id IS NOT NULL THEN $6::text ELSE l.crm_enqueued_requirement END,
      crm_enqueued_record_hash = CASE
        WHEN i.id IS NOT NULL AND NULLIF($9::text, '') IS NOT NULL THEN NULLIF($8::text, '')
        ELSE l.crm_enqueued_record_hash
      END,
      crm_checked_source_hash = COALESCE(NULLIF($9::text, ''), l.crm_checked_source_hash),
      crm_blocked_reason = CASE
        WHEN i.id IS NOT NULL THEN NULL
        WHEN NULLIF($7::text, '') IS NOT NULL THEN $7::text
        WHEN NULLIF($9::text, '') IS NOT NULL THEN NULL
        ELSE l.crm_blocked_reason
      END
  FROM expected x
  LEFT JOIN inserted i ON i.lead_id = x.id
  WHERE l.id = x.id
    AND (i.id IS NOT NULL OR NULLIF($7::text, '') IS NOT NULL OR NULLIF($9::text, '') IS NOT NULL)
  RETURNING l.id, l.crm_blocked_reason
)
SELECT
  $1::bigint AS lead_id,
  EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM inserted) AS enqueued,
  (SELECT i.event_id FROM inserted i) AS event_id,
  (SELECT lu.crm_blocked_reason FROM lead_update lu) AS blocked_reason;

-- Select chat messages to announce to the CRM as message.new (stage C, read
-- side). Protocol revision 1.2 only: under any other revision it returns no row.
-- p1 protocol revision, p2 CRM_EVENTS_SINCE (ISO timestamp), p3 id prefix,
-- p4 batch size.
--
-- A message is a candidate when its conversation was already announced to the
-- CRM by a delivered lead.qualified event (so the CRM knows the conversation),
-- it was created at or after CRM_EVENTS_SINCE, it is not deleted, and it has no
-- message.new event yet. Incoming messages always qualify; outgoing ones only
-- once actually sent (delivery_status 'sent', the same rule the conversation
-- history uses), so a queued, failed, cancelled or unknown send never reaches
-- the CRM. Messages of a conversation before its lead qualified are included:
-- the seller sees the whole chat. sender_type is NOT NULL and limited to
-- customer, bot, human and system since migration 018; the builder maps it and
-- blocks anything else. A human reply carries the crm_user_id of the seller
-- assigned to the conversation's lead. sent_at is the provider timestamp when
-- known, else the row creation time, as UTC with milliseconds and Z.
-- Messages blocked on a previous pass go last so they cannot starve the batch.
WITH announced AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT DISTINCT substring(e.conversation_id FROM '-conversation-([0-9]+)$')::bigint AS conversation_id
  FROM crm_events e
  WHERE $1::text = '1.2'
    AND e.event_type = 'lead.qualified'
    AND e.status = 'delivered'
    AND e.conversation_id LIKE 'wa-' || $3::text || '-conversation-%'
)
SELECT
  m.id AS message_id,
  m.conversation_id,
  m.direction,
  m.sender_type,
  m.message_type,
  m.text_body,
  COALESCE(
    attachment.filename,
    NULLIF(btrim(m.raw_payload->>'fileName'), ''),
    NULLIF(btrim(m.raw_payload#>>'{data,message,documentMessage,fileName}'), ''),
    NULLIF(btrim(m.raw_payload#>>'{message,documentMessage,fileName}'), '')
  ) AS file_name,
  to_char(COALESCE(m.external_timestamp, m.created_at) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"') AS sent_at,
  CASE WHEN m.direction = 'outgoing' AND m.sender_type = 'human' THEN s.crm_user_id::text END AS crm_user_id
FROM announced a
JOIN messages m ON m.conversation_id = a.conversation_id
JOIN conversations c ON c.id = m.conversation_id
LEFT JOIN leads l ON l.id = COALESCE(c.lead_id, m.lead_id)
LEFT JOIN sellers s ON s.id = l.assigned_seller_id AND s.deleted_at IS NULL
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT NULLIF(btrim(ma.filename), '') AS filename
  FROM message_attachments ma
  WHERE ma.message_id = m.id
    AND NULLIF(btrim(ma.filename), '') IS NOT NULL
  ORDER BY ma.id
  LIMIT 1
) attachment ON TRUE
LEFT JOIN crm_message_blocks b ON b.message_id = m.id
WHERE m.deleted_at IS NULL
  AND m.created_at >= $2::timestamptz
  AND (m.direction = 'incoming' OR (m.direction = 'outgoing' AND m.delivery_status = 'sent'))
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM crm_events e
    WHERE e.message_id = m.id
      AND e.event_type = 'message.new'
  )
ORDER BY (b.message_id IS NOT NULL), m.created_at, m.id
LIMIT COALESCE(NULLIF($4::text, '')::integer, 100);

-- Enqueue message.new events (stage C, write side).
-- p1 JSON array of { message_id, event_id, conversation_id, body,
-- blocked_reason } built by Build Message Events.
--
-- A row with a body and no blocked reason becomes a pending crm_events row
-- (lead_id NULL, revision 1) and clears any earlier block of that message. A
-- blocked row is recorded in crm_message_blocks instead, so the next pass sees
-- it last and retries it. Unique event_id and (message_id, event_type) make a
-- re-run or a concurrent pass a no-op, never a duplicate.
WITH input AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT x.message_id, x.event_id, x.conversation_id, x.body, NULLIF(x.blocked_reason, '') AS blocked_reason
  FROM jsonb_to_recordset(COALESCE(NULLIF($1::text, ''), '[]')::jsonb)
    AS x(message_id BIGINT, event_id TEXT, conversation_id TEXT, body TEXT, blocked_reason TEXT)
  JOIN messages m ON m.id = x.message_id
),
inserted AS (
  INSERT INTO crm_events (event_id, event_type, conversation_id, message_id, revision, body)
  SELECT i.event_id, 'message.new', i.conversation_id, i.message_id, 1, i.body
  FROM input i
  WHERE i.blocked_reason IS NULL
    AND NULLIF(i.body, '') IS NOT NULL
    AND NULLIF(i.event_id, '') IS NOT NULL
    AND NULLIF(i.conversation_id, '') IS NOT NULL
  ORDER BY i.message_id
  ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
  RETURNING message_id
),
unblocked AS (
  DELETE FROM crm_message_blocks b
  USING inserted i
  WHERE b.message_id = i.message_id
  RETURNING b.message_id
),
blocked AS (
  INSERT INTO crm_message_blocks (message_id, reason)
  SELECT i.message_id, i.blocked_reason
  FROM input i
  WHERE i.blocked_reason IS NOT NULL
  ON CONFLICT (message_id) DO UPDATE
  SET reason = EXCLUDED.reason,
      updated_at = NOW()
  WHERE crm_message_blocks.reason IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.reason
  RETURNING message_id
)
SELECT
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM inserted)::integer AS enqueued,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM blocked)::integer AS blocked,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM unblocked)::integer AS unblocked;

-- Select ownership changes to announce to the CRM as ownership.taken /
-- ownership.released (stage D, read side). Protocol revision 1.2 only: under
-- any other revision it returns no row.
-- p1 protocol revision, p2 CRM_EVENTS_SINCE (ISO timestamp), p3 id prefix,
-- p4 batch size.
--
-- One row of crm_ownership_changes (migration 040) is one version of the
-- conversation's ownership. A change is a candidate when its conversation was
-- already announced by a delivered lead.qualified event (the CRM knows the
-- conversation), it happened at or after CRM_EVENTS_SINCE, and it has no
-- crm_events row yet. Changes from before the lead qualified are included, in
-- version order, like the chat history: the CRM keeps the newest version and
-- acknowledges older ones. crm_user_id is the CRM id of the seller who took
-- the chat (NULL when unmapped, which ownership.taken allows). Changes blocked
-- on a previous pass go last so they cannot starve the batch.
WITH announced AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT DISTINCT substring(e.conversation_id FROM '-conversation-([0-9]+)$')::bigint AS conversation_id
  FROM crm_events e
  WHERE $1::text = '1.2'
    AND e.event_type = 'lead.qualified'
    AND e.status = 'delivered'
    AND e.conversation_id LIKE 'wa-' || $3::text || '-conversation-%'
)
SELECT
  ch.id AS change_id,
  ch.conversation_id,
  ch.ownership_version,
  ch.change_kind,
  ch.source,
  ch.reason,
  CASE WHEN ch.change_kind = 'taken' THEN s.crm_user_id::text END AS crm_user_id
FROM announced a
JOIN crm_ownership_changes ch ON ch.conversation_id = a.conversation_id
LEFT JOIN sellers s ON s.id = ch.seller_id AND s.deleted_at IS NULL
WHERE ch.changed_at >= $2::timestamptz
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM crm_events e
    WHERE e.ownership_change_id = ch.id
  )
ORDER BY (ch.crm_blocked_reason IS NOT NULL), ch.changed_at, ch.conversation_id, ch.ownership_version
LIMIT COALESCE(NULLIF($4::text, '')::integer, 100);

-- Enqueue ownership.taken / ownership.released events (stage D, write side).
-- p1 JSON array of { change_id, event_id, conversation_id, event_type, body,
-- blocked_reason } built by Build Ownership Events.
--
-- A row with a body and no blocked reason becomes a pending crm_events row
-- (lead_id NULL, revision 1, ownership_change_id set) and clears any earlier
-- block of that change. A blocked row records its reason on the change, so the
-- next pass sees it last and retries it. Unique event_id and
-- ownership_change_id make a re-run or a concurrent pass a no-op.
WITH input AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT x.change_id, x.event_id, x.conversation_id, x.event_type, x.body, NULLIF(x.blocked_reason, '') AS blocked_reason
  FROM jsonb_to_recordset(COALESCE(NULLIF($1::text, ''), '[]')::jsonb)
    AS x(change_id BIGINT, event_id TEXT, conversation_id TEXT, event_type TEXT, body TEXT, blocked_reason TEXT)
  JOIN crm_ownership_changes ch ON ch.id = x.change_id
),
inserted AS (
  INSERT INTO crm_events (event_id, event_type, conversation_id, ownership_change_id, revision, body)
  SELECT i.event_id, i.event_type, i.conversation_id, i.change_id, 1, i.body
  FROM input i
  WHERE i.blocked_reason IS NULL
    AND i.event_type IN ('ownership.taken', 'ownership.released')
    AND NULLIF(i.body, '') IS NOT NULL
    AND NULLIF(i.event_id, '') IS NOT NULL
    AND NULLIF(i.conversation_id, '') IS NOT NULL
  ORDER BY i.change_id
  ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
  RETURNING ownership_change_id
),
unblocked AS (
  UPDATE crm_ownership_changes ch
  SET crm_blocked_reason = NULL
  FROM inserted i
  WHERE ch.id = i.ownership_change_id
    AND ch.crm_blocked_reason IS NOT NULL
  RETURNING ch.id
),
blocked AS (
  UPDATE crm_ownership_changes ch
  SET crm_blocked_reason = i.blocked_reason
  FROM input i
  WHERE ch.id = i.change_id
    AND i.blocked_reason IS NOT NULL
    AND ch.crm_blocked_reason IS DISTINCT FROM i.blocked_reason
  RETURNING ch.id
)
SELECT
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM inserted)::integer AS enqueued,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM blocked)::integer AS blocked,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM unblocked)::integer AS unblocked;

-- Claim due CRM events for delivery (stage B).
-- p1 batch size, p2 stale processing seconds.
--
-- Due pending rows and processing rows whose claim went stale (the worker died
-- mid-delivery) are claimed together with a fresh claim_token; the old token
-- can no longer complete. Re-sending a stale row is safe: the CRM answers a
-- duplicate event_id with its stored 200 result. The body is returned exactly
-- as stored and must be sent as-is. event_type tells delivery which success
-- shape to expect (lead.qualified or message.new).
WITH candidates AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT e.id
  FROM crm_events e
  WHERE (e.status = 'pending' AND e.next_attempt_at <= NOW())
     OR (e.status = 'processing'
         AND e.locked_at < NOW() - (COALESCE(NULLIF($2::text, '')::integer, 900) * INTERVAL '1 second'))
  ORDER BY e.next_attempt_at, e.id
  LIMIT COALESCE(NULLIF($1::text, '')::integer, 20)
  FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
),
claimed AS (
  UPDATE crm_events e
  SET status = 'processing',
      claim_token = gen_random_uuid(),
      locked_at = NOW(),
      attempt_count = e.attempt_count + 1,
      last_error = CASE WHEN e.status = 'processing' THEN 'stale_processing_reclaimed' ELSE e.last_error END,
      updated_at = NOW()
  FROM candidates c
  WHERE e.id = c.id
  RETURNING e.id, e.event_id, e.event_type, e.claim_token, e.attempt_count, e.body, e.lead_id, e.message_id, e.revision
)
SELECT
  id AS crm_event_id,
  event_id,
  event_type,
  claim_token::text AS claim_token,
  attempt_count,
  body,
  lead_id,
  message_id,
  revision
FROM claimed
ORDER BY id;

-- Complete one claimed CRM event (stage B).
-- p1 crm_event_id, p2 claim_token, p3 outcome (delivered | retry | parked),
-- p4 http status, p5 error, p6 response json, p7 crm_customer_id,
-- p8 crm_opportunity_id, p9 retry delay seconds.
--
-- Only the holder of the current claim_token may complete. delivered stores
-- the CRM result and writes the CRM ids on the lead unless a newer revision
-- was already delivered (a message.new row has no lead and carries no ids, so
-- it never touches leads); retry returns the row to pending at now + delay;
-- anything else parks it for reconciliation. The body is never touched.
WITH authorized AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT e.id
  FROM crm_events e
  WHERE e.id = $1::bigint
    AND e.status = 'processing'
    AND e.claim_token = NULLIF($2::text, '')::uuid
  FOR UPDATE
),
event_update AS (
  UPDATE crm_events e
  SET status = CASE $3::text WHEN 'delivered' THEN 'delivered' WHEN 'retry' THEN 'pending' ELSE 'parked' END,
      claim_token = NULL,
      locked_at = NULL,
      last_http_status = NULLIF($4::text, '')::integer,
      last_error = CASE WHEN $3::text = 'delivered' THEN NULL ELSE COALESCE(NULLIF($5::text, ''), 'unspecified') END,
      response = COALESCE(NULLIF($6::text, '')::jsonb, e.response),
      next_attempt_at = CASE
        WHEN $3::text = 'retry'
          THEN NOW() + (GREATEST(COALESCE(NULLIF($9::text, '')::integer, 30), 1) * INTERVAL '1 second')
        ELSE e.next_attempt_at
      END,
      delivered_at = CASE WHEN $3::text = 'delivered' THEN NOW() ELSE e.delivered_at END,
      updated_at = NOW()
  FROM authorized a
  WHERE e.id = a.id
  RETURNING e.id, e.event_id, e.lead_id, e.revision, e.status
),
lead_update AS (
  UPDATE leads l
  SET crm_customer_id = NULLIF($7::text, '')::uuid,
      crm_opportunity_id = NULLIF($8::text, '')::uuid,
      crm_revision = u.revision
  FROM event_update u
  WHERE u.status = 'delivered'
    AND l.id = u.lead_id
    AND u.revision >= COALESCE(l.crm_revision, 0)
    AND NULLIF($7::text, '') IS NOT NULL
    AND NULLIF($8::text, '') IS NOT NULL
  RETURNING l.id
)
SELECT
  u.id AS crm_event_id,
  u.event_id,
  u.status,
  EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM lead_update) AS lead_updated
FROM event_update u;
